concepts.preferred_label: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) Pneumonia
support_spans: SARS-CoV-2 infection was confirmed by nasopharyngeal PCR
bilateral ground‐glass opacities with lower-lung predominance
concepts.why: The patient has a confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, a history of fever and cough, and bilateral ground-glass opacities on chest CT, which are all consistent with SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia.
The patient has elevated WBC and CRP, and a prolonged APTT, which are all consistent with DIC.
The patient has a history of fever and cough, and is under deep sedation, which increases the risk of VAP.
The patient has a history of fever and cough, elevated WBC, and elevated CRP, which are all consistent with sepsis.

support_spans: diffuse edema of the intestine, including the transverse colon
concepts.why: The patient has diffuse edema of the intestine, which may be related to AKI.

rationales.F02: The patient's 4-day history of fever and cough is consistent with a respiratory infection, which could be related to SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia or ventilator-associated pneumonia.
rationales.F03: The confirmation of SARS-CoV-2 infection by nasopharyngeal PCR strongly supports the diagnosis of SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia.
rationales.F08: The elevated white blood cell count is a non-specific indicator of infection or inflammation, which could be related to SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia, ventilator-associated pneumonia, or sepsis.
rationales.F09: The elevated C-reactive protein level is a non-specific indicator of inflammation, which could be related to SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia, ventilator-associated pneumonia, or sepsis.
rationales.F10: The presence of bilateral ground-glass opacities with lower-lung predominance on chest CT is consistent with SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia.
rationales.F11: The diffuse edema of the intestine could be related to sepsis or acute kidney injury.
rationales.F12: The prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) is consistent with disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC).
